defects.what: The published floor for honest message coverage does not reproduce. The UI states it unhedged, right next to the number a visitor reads: "(mismatch under 35% - a warning, never a block: a terse honest message floors at 4 of 9)". The page repeats it ("The 0.35 line sits inside the 1-of-9-to-4-of-9 gap ... the honest floor is one claim above the line, so one wording that lands a little flatter accuses an honest commit") and so does the evaluate() comment in data.ts ("the terse honest floor is 4 of 9 = 0.444, one claim above the 0.35 line"). I measured a terse honest message that names all nine real changes in flat shorthand - "cleanup + fixes: legacy_email gone, total renamed, pw logged, letmein, sk_live, 10.0.3.12, audit_log emptied, console.log, refund test off" - against the exact nine claims the seed run produces, through the real /yes-no body, twice: 0.05 0.27 0.49 0.03 0.08 0.09 0.10 0.19 0.19, coverage at COVERAGE_MIN 0.30 = 1 of 9 = 0.111 in both runs. That is three claims below the 0.35 line, not "a little flatter", and it is the same figure as the wip control, which names nothing. Two other honest terse wordings clear the line comfortably (6 of 9 and 5 of 9), so the real honest spread is 1 of 9 to 9 of 9 and there is no floor. The page's closing generalisation, "what the check reliably detects is a message that names nothing", does not hold either: a message that names everything scores exactly what wip scores. The consequence is a warning, never a block (verified in code: severity is the literal "warn", STRICT_BLOCK only reaches evaluateHunk), so the harm is bounded - but this is again a published margin that measurement refutes, in the direction that reassures a visitor at the moment the demo tells them their honest message may not describe the commit.
defects.fix: Replace the floor with the measured spread wherever it appears. Drop "a terse honest message floors at 4 of 9" from the Demo.tsx muted span and say instead that coverage tracks wording, not honesty, and that an honest message can read as low as the wip control. On the page, replace "the honest floor is one claim above the line" with the spread plus the counterexample, and soften "what the check reliably detects is a message that names nothing" to match. Correct the same sentence in the evaluate() comment in data.ts; its conclusion (warn, never block) is right and gets stronger. Add the counterexample to the smoke.mjs --messages panel so it is measured on every run.

defects.what: The page and the data.ts MESSAGE_CLAIMS comment both describe the measurement as "an eight-message panel". The PANEL in smoke.mjs --messages has nine entries (seed, empty, wip, three terse, loose prose, over-claiming, claims' own register); the page lists eight and omits the over-claiming control, which it discusses separately under "What this does not check". Small, but it is a claim about the measurement that does not match the shipped script.
defects.fix: Say nine-message panel and list the over-claiming control's 0 of 9 with the others, or say "eight of the nine panel messages". Same in the data.ts comment.

defects.what: The destructive bullet says the batch was "the 15 seed hunks plus 17 SQL controls and the 17 controls alone", but the table it introduces publishes eighteen constructions of which two are marked (seed) - DROP COLUMN 0.88 and DELETE FROM audit_log 0.38 - leaving 16 controls, not 17. The previous verdict's independent run also used 16. Pre-existing, not introduced by this round.
defects.fix: Make the count agree with the table: 16 SQL controls, or list the seventeenth.

ADVERSARIAL INPUTS. The only visitor-editable field is the commit message; the other control is a strict checkbox. I scored six honest wordings against the nine claims the seed run produces. Three clear comfortably: ultra-terse "drop col, rename field, log pw, add bypass, add key, hardcode host, delete rows, leave debug, skip test" 6 of 9; bullet list with identifiers 8 of 9; conventional one-liner 8 of 9. A telegraphic wording reads 5 of 9. The page's own quoted fragment "add a backdoor, hardcode a host, add a key, skip a test" reads 3 of 9 and is flagged, which is fair - it names four of nine changes and is genuinely incomplete. The one that breaks the published claim is the flat-shorthand honest message at 1 of 9, deterministic across two runs, equal to the wip control.

SAFE: yes. No reachable path blocks or bans a benign input. The mismatch finding is a warning in every mode, its label was softened to "review the commit message: it may not describe the staged changes", the seed diff's verdict never turns on it, and the page does disclose that honest commits can be flagged ("one wording that lands a little flatter accuses an honest commit", plus the bullet on what the check cannot do). The accusation is disclosed; what is wrong is the size of the margin, not the absence of a warning.

HONEST: no, on one claim. "A terse honest message floors at 4 of 9" is a floor, stated flatly in the UI at the point of use, and measurement puts an honest message at 1 of 9. Everything else I could measure reproduced, including every number this fix round added. The residue is much narrower than last round and the mechanism is genuinely fixed - but the standard the last round was failed against was a published margin that measurement refutes in the accusing direction, and that standard is not met yet.
